THING.description: root: any node type is-a THING

METHOD.description: a named modeling approach/theory/law/model (e.g. μ(I) rheology, kinetic theory, NGF, DEM, RFT)

PARAMETER.description: a named physical quantity/constant/coefficient in equations (e.g. μ, I, d, P, τ, g, ρ_s, T, A, ξ, μ_s, b)

PHENOMENON.description: a physical effect/behavior methods capture (e.g. nonlocal creep, thin-body strengthening, secondary rheology, segregation, clogging)

PROPERTY.description: a generic physical property/quantity not fitting the above (kept for residual cases)

DATA.description: A dataset, data artifact, or collection of data instances used for training, evaluation, or analysis.

constitutive_law.description: a constitutive law relating output quantity/quantities to >=1 input quantity (n-ary)
constitutive_law.semantic_boundary: a FORMAL/QUANTITATIVE law output=f(inputs+params), stated as a formula or explicit functional relation. NOT a prose 'X depends on Y' (that is influences), NOT a definition (defines), NOT a measurement setup (measures).

influences.description: one quantity influences / depends on >=1 target quantity (n-ary, general dependence)
influences.semantic_boundary: X functionally depends on / varies with Y (a genuine causal or scaling dependence). NOT a co-listing of parallel items (composed_of), NOT a classification (defines), NOT 'we tested X' (measures), NOT 'X is part of Y' (composed_of).

defines.description: one entity is defined-as / identified-with / named-by another (definitional identity, n-ary)
defines.semantic_boundary: a DEFINITIONAL identity: X is defined as / is / denotes / is named / is classified into Y. NOT a structural part-of (composed_of), NOT a functional dependence (influences). 'X is analogous to Y' is a CLAIM not a definition.

composed_of.description: one whole is composed-of / part-of >=1 component (n-ary composition)
composed_of.semantic_boundary: STRUCTURAL composition: parts that make up a whole (model A = B + C). NOT classification (defines), NOT 'X has control params' (influences), NOT experimental setup description, NOT 'we tested X by doing Y'.

measures.description: a quantity is measured by / characterizes >=1 measure
measures.semantic_boundary: a measurement/evaluation relation: X is measured/evaluated by instrument/method Y. NOT a functional law (constitutive_law), NOT a dependence (influences).

claim_relation.semantic_boundary: a DISCOURSE relation between claims/findings (supports/contrasts/outperforms). NOT a method-to-method development (extends/improves/compares — those are evolution), NOT a measurement (measures).

extends.semantic_boundary: X GENERALIZES Y (X extends Y's scope/regime/params; X is a direct technical extension of Y). NOT improves (X need not be more accurate, just broader), NOT background (X is a direct technical inheritance, not a motivation citation), NOT claim_relation (this is method-to-method).

improves.description: X improves Y's accuracy/applicability, resolving Y's limitation
improves.semantic_boundary: X RESOLVES a limitation of Y (X is more accurate/applicable BECAUSE it fixes something Y fails at; first-principles vs phenomenological = improves). NOT compares (X is NOT a parallel different-mechanism alternative; X builds on Y and is better), NOT extends (X is better not just broader).

compares.semantic_boundary: A and B are put side by side: either (i) PARALLEL different-mechanism alternatives with overlapping scope (both model the same phenomenon, different assumptions), or (ii) THEORY-vs-EXPERIMENT / prediction-vs-observation validation ('data compared with predictions', 'simulations agree with experiments', 'in contrast with'), or (iii) equivalence/contrast of formulations ('equivalent', 'the same as', 'rather than'). NOT improves (neither fixes the other's limitation), NOT extends (neither generalizes the other).

replaces.semantic_boundary: X SUBSTITUTES Y outright (X is used INSTEAD of Y; Y is retired). NOT improves (replaces = Y is gone, improves = Y still used + X better).

adapts.description: X adapts Y to a new scenario
adapts.semantic_boundary: X PORTS Y to a NEW scenario/regime/domain Y wasn't designed for (adaptation of Y's mechanism). NOT extends (adapts = new scenario, extends = broader scope within same setting).

background.semantic_boundary: X cites Y as MOTIVATION/prior context only (Y inspired X but X is NOT a direct technical extension/inheritance of Y). NOT extends (no direct technical lineage), NOT improves (no limitation fix).

experiment_with_alternatives.description: X is an experiment that compares/uses multiple alternative techniques Y1, Y2... (the experiment itself is the subject, alternatives are objects)
experiment_with_alternatives.semantic_boundary: Use when the experiment itself is the subject and the alternatives are its objects; NOT when listing methods without an experimental comparison, or when the experiment is the object of a method.

uses_tool.description: X uses Y as a tool/instrument to perform a task (Y is a software library, toolkit, or utility employed by X).
uses_tool.semantic_boundary: Use this pattern only when Y is explicitly a tool/library/utility that X employs to perform a task, not when X and Y are merely co-listed, compared, or when Y is a component, input, or output of X.

trains_with_data.description: X (a model/method) is trained on data produced/augmented by Y (another method).
trains_with_data.semantic_boundary: Apply when a method is explicitly trained on data produced or augmented by another method, not when they merely share a dataset or are jointly evaluated.

dataset_comparison.description: Multiple datasets are compared/used as benchmarks in an evaluation (the datasets are the subjects being compared).
dataset_comparison.semantic_boundary: Use when two datasets are explicitly compared or benchmarked against each other, not when they are merely co-listed or used together in a pipeline.

improves_over<claim>.description: X improves over Y in terms of performance or effectiveness (X yields better results than Y, often as a baseline comparison).
improves_over<claim>.semantic_boundary: Use when one method is explicitly shown to outperform another in a comparison, not when they are merely alternatives, complements, or listed together.

may_differ_for.description: X (a finding/result) may differ or show different tendencies for Y (a different domain/language/regime).
may_differ_for.semantic_boundary: Use when a finding is explicitly contrasted across domains/languages/regimes, not when X merely occurs in Y or when Y is a cause/effect of X.

contrasts_with.description: X (a method/approach) is contrasted/differentiated from Y (another method/approach) based on a fundamental difference in mechanism or setting.
contrasts_with.semantic_boundary: Use only when the text explicitly contrasts two methods/approaches by mechanism or setting, not when it merely compares outcomes, lists alternatives, or describes one method’s components.

step_of.description: X is a step/phase in the procedural pipeline of method Y (Y's workflow is composed of sequential steps X1, X2...).
step_of.semantic_boundary: Apply when X is a named phase or stage within Y’s procedural workflow, not when X is a sub-method, component, or merely a prerequisite for Y.

ablation_comparison.description: X (a method variant) is compared against Y (another variant of the same method) to isolate the effect of a specific component or design choice, typically in an ablation study.
ablation_comparison.semantic_boundary: Use when the comparison isolates a single component or design choice between two variants of the same method, NOT when comparing different methods or overall performance.

creates_data.description: X (a method) creates/generates data Y (a dataset or data artifact) as part of its operation or output.
creates_data.semantic_boundary: Applies when a method explicitly produces or outputs data, not when it merely uses, transforms, or is associated with data in a pipeline.

uses_representation.description: X (a method) uses Y (a representation/formal structure) as a component or basis for its operation.
uses_representation.semantic_boundary: X uses Y as a structural component or basis for operation, NOT Y being a subtype, instance, or causal trigger of X.

based_on_perspective.description: X (a method/approach) is based on or motivated by Y (a perspective, principle, or conceptual framework), where Y provides the conceptual foundation but is not a direct technical predecessor or a mere background citation.
based_on_perspective.semantic_boundary: Apply when Y is the conceptual foundation for X, not a technical predecessor (use based_on_previous_work) or a mere background citation (use cites).

roots_in.description: X (a method/approach) has its conceptual or theoretical roots in Y (a principle, technique, or framework), where Y provides the foundational idea but X is not a direct technical extension or implementation of Y.
roots_in.semantic_boundary: Use when X conceptually inherits from Y but isn’t a direct implementation, extension, or variant of Y—not for shared lineage, co-citation, or X being built on Y’s code.

complementary_approaches.description: X and Y are complementary approaches that address the same problem from different angles, where each exploits a different aspect or mechanism to solve the same issue.
complementary_approaches.semantic_boundary: X and Y are distinct methods solving the same problem via different mechanisms; NOT co-listing, NOT one being a subtype or variant of the other.

produces_erroneous_output.description: X (a method/process) produces or generates Y (erroneous, incorrect, or low-quality output/data) as a byproduct or consequence of its operation.
produces_erroneous_output.semantic_boundary: Applies when X actively generates Y as a flawed result; NOT when X merely contains, uses, or is associated with Y, nor when Y is a deliberate intended output.

tradeoff_comparison.description: X and Y are compared in terms of a tradeoff between different performance dimensions (e.g., accuracy vs. speed), where each option excels on a different axis.
tradeoff_comparison.semantic_boundary: Use when two methods are explicitly pitted against each other on different performance axes, not when one method simply outperforms another on a single metric.

interplays_with.description: X (a method/schedule) can be combined or integrated with Y (another method) to yield benefits, where X is orthogonal to or compatible with Y.
interplays_with.semantic_boundary: X = interplays_with when methods are explicitly combined or integrated for mutual benefit, NOT mere co-occurrence, sequential use, or one method being a subtype of another.

compatible_with.description: X (a method/approach) is compatible with or can be integrated with Y (another method/approach) without conflict, where X's design does not interfere with Y's operation. This is a weaker relation than interplays_with (which implies mutual benefit from combination) — here the claim is only that X does not hinder or conflict with Y, not that combining them yields benefits.
compatible_with.semantic_boundary: Use only when the claim is that one method does not conflict with another; do not use if the methods are merely listed together, or if combining them yields a benefit (use interplays_with).

generalizes_across.description: X (a method/approach) generalizes from Y (a specific setting/level) to Z (a broader setting/level), where the generalization is about transferring capability across different scopes or granularities.
generalizes_across.semantic_boundary: Generalization across scopes/levels, NOT mere analogy, similarity, or transfer between distinct tasks—X must explicitly extend from a narrower to a broader setting.

explores_setting.description: X (a work/study) explores Y (a setting/regime) that involves Z (a set of tasks/approaches), where the setting is the context and the tasks are what's being addressed within it.
explores_setting.semantic_boundary: Use when the work explicitly situates tasks within a named setting/regime; not for mere co-occurrence of work and tasks without that contextual framing.

related_to_work.description: X (a work/method) is related to Y (another work/method) in that they share a common goal or approach, but without being a direct extension, improvement, or contrast.
related_to_work.semantic_boundary: Apply when X and Y are independently presented as sharing a goal or approach, not when one is built on, improves, or directly opposes the other.

defines_problem_setting.description: X (a work/challenge) defines or establishes Y (a problem setting/regime) that involves Z (a set of tasks or properties), where the setting is the conceptual framing and the tasks are what's addressed within it.
defines_problem_setting.semantic_boundary: Applies when a work explicitly frames a problem setting and names the tasks within it, not when it merely lists properties or defines a single concept.

formulates_task.description: X (a work/challenge) formulates or establishes Y (a task) as a general formulation, where Y is the conceptual framing for the work's approach.
formulates_task.semantic_boundary: Use when X frames Y as the overarching task or goal, not when X merely describes, evaluates, or lists Y as a component.

focuses_on_limitation.description: X (a work/approach) focuses on or addresses Y (a limitation/gap in existing work), where Y is the specific shortcoming that motivates X's contribution.
focuses_on_limitation.semantic_boundary: Use when X explicitly names or targets Y as a problem to solve; not when Y is merely a context, background, or motivation for X.

shares_size_with.description: X (a dataset/split) shares the same size or scale as Y (another dataset/split), where the two are comparable in magnitude.
shares_size_with.semantic_boundary: Use when comparing dataset sizes or scales directly; not for sample counts, row counts, or storage size, and not for qualitative similarity in content or structure.

lists_alternative_methods.description: X (a work/study) presents or lists multiple alternative methods Y1, Y2... as options for addressing the same problem, where the methods are described as distinct approaches but not explicitly compared, contrasted, or evaluated against each other in the text.
lists_alternative_methods.semantic_boundary: Apply when a work explicitly lists distinct methods as options for one problem, without comparing or evaluating them; not for methods that are contrasted, ranked, or jointly applied.

correlated_performance.description: X (a method/approach) and Y (another method/approach) show correlated performance or benefit across tasks, where the correlation is a statistical relationship between their relative improvements or effectiveness.
correlated_performance.semantic_boundary: Apply when two methods’ performance metrics are statistically correlated across tasks, not when they merely co-occur, are compared, or one causes the other.

applies_after.description: X (a method/technique) is applied after Y (another method/technique) in a sequential pipeline, where the order matters and X operates on the output of Y, but X is not a step within Y's own procedural workflow.
applies_after.semantic_boundary: X is applied after Y in a sequential pipeline, NOT a co-listing, NOT a step within Y’s own workflow, and NOT a mere ordering of independent steps.

introduces_benchmark.description: X (a work/challenge) introduces or establishes Y (a benchmark/task setup) that standardizes or defines Z (a set of tasks or evaluation protocols), where the benchmark is the primary contribution and the tasks are what's addressed within it.
introduces_benchmark.semantic_boundary: Applies when the benchmark is the paper’s main contribution, not when the work merely uses or evaluates an existing benchmark.

acknowledges_contributor.description: X (a work/team) acknowledges or thanks Y (a person/team/entity) for providing or making available Z (a resource/tool/data), where the acknowledgment is a credit for contribution rather than a technical dependency or usage.
acknowledges_contributor.semantic_boundary: Acknowledgment is credit for contribution, not a technical dependency, usage, or co-listing; the resource must be explicitly thanked or credited, not merely referenced or employed.

follows_methodology.description: X (a work/method) follows or adopts the methodology/approach of Y (another work/method), where Y's procedure is replicated or adapted by X without being a direct technical extension or improvement.
follows_methodology.semantic_boundary: X follows Y’s methodology/approach, but does NOT extend, improve, or technically build on Y; use only when Y’s procedure is replicated or adapted, not superseded.

performs_similarly_with_exception.description: X (a method) performs similarly to Y (another method) overall, but with a specific exception or condition where one performs better.
performs_similarly_with_exception.semantic_boundary: Use only when the comparison explicitly names a specific exception or condition where one method outperforms the other; not for general similarity or unqualified performance claims.

cost_effectiveness_comparison.description: X (a method) is compared with Y (another method) in terms of cost-effectiveness, where the comparison involves both resource expenditure (time, cost) and performance outcomes.
cost_effectiveness_comparison.semantic_boundary: Use when a claim explicitly weighs both cost/resource use and effectiveness/outcome of two methods; not for mere performance comparison, cost-only, or co-listing.

evaluates_against.description: X (a work/benchmark) evaluates or assesses Y (a set of methods/techniques) against Z (a baseline or standard), where the evaluation is the primary activity and the baseline provides a reference point for comparison.
evaluates_against.semantic_boundary: Use when a benchmark explicitly compares methods against a fixed baseline; NOT when methods are merely co-listed or evaluated without a reference standard.

reports_statistics.description: X (a method/toolkit) reports or provides Y (statistics, metrics, or measurements) as part of its output or documentation, where Y is a set of quantitative summaries that X communicates to users.
reports_statistics.semantic_boundary: Applies when a method explicitly outputs or documents quantitative summaries; not when it merely measures, evaluates, or lists properties without reporting them.

determines_sample_size.description: X (a method/approach) determines or establishes the optimal configuration of Y (a set of sample size parameters) in the context of Z (a benchmark/setting), where the configuration involves trade-offs between multiple parameters (e.g., number of episodes vs. examples per episode) under resource constraints.
determines_sample_size.semantic_boundary: Applies when a method explicitly sets sample size parameters (e.g., episodes, examples) via trade-offs under constraints, not when merely reporting or comparing fixed sample sizes.

inspired_by_technique.description: X (a method/approach) is inspired by or draws upon Y (a technique/methodology), where Y provides conceptual or methodological inspiration but X is not a direct implementation or extension of Y.
inspired_by_technique.semantic_boundary: Apply when X explicitly cites Y as conceptual inspiration, not when X is a direct extension, implementation, or variant of Y.

based_on_pretraining.description: X (a method/approach) is based on or derived from Y (a pretrained model/approach), where Y's pretraining provides the foundation for X's design or initialization.
based_on_pretraining.semantic_boundary: Use when Y’s pretraining directly enables or initializes X; not when X merely extends, evaluates, or co-occurs with Y.

has_primitive_ability.description: X (a model/method) has a primitive or basic ability to recognize/process Y (a set of patterns, shapes, or relationships), where the ability is foundational but limited.
has_primitive_ability.semantic_boundary: Use when a method is credited with a specific, limited capability (e.g., recognizing shapes), NOT for general performance claims or co-occurrence of unrelated traits.

may_benefit_from.description: X (a method/approach) may benefit from leveraging or incorporating Y (another method/approach), where the benefit is potential or suggested but not yet demonstrated or implemented.
may_benefit_from.semantic_boundary: Applies when a paper suggests a potential benefit of combining methods, but does not demonstrate or implement it; NOT for proven improvements, comparisons, or mere co-occurrence.

more_expressive_than.description: X (a language/method) is more expressive than Y (another language/method), where expressiveness refers to the range or complexity of concepts that can be represented or expressed.
more_expressive_than.semantic_boundary: Use only when claiming one method’s expressive range exceeds another’s, not for general superiority, compatibility, or equivalence.

approximately_equivalent_to.description: X (a method/approach) is approximately equivalent to Y (another method/approach) in terms of underlying mechanism or formal structure, where the equivalence is approximate or in a specific sense.
approximately_equivalent_to.semantic_boundary: Applies when two methods are claimed to be interchangeable in mechanism or form, not when one is a variant, extension, or replacement of the other.

serves_purpose.description: X (a method/approach) serves or fulfills Y (a purpose, goal, or function), where Y is the intended outcome or benefit that X provides.
serves_purpose.semantic_boundary: Use when X is an action or approach explicitly aimed at achieving Y as its goal; not when X merely causes, enables, or is associated with Y.

uses_technique.description: X (a method/model) uses Y (a technique/approach) as part of its operation, where Y is a specific technique employed by X but not necessarily a tool or component.
uses_technique.semantic_boundary: X = a method/model actively employing a technique in its operation, NOT a co-listing, comparison, or where the technique is merely a component/tool.

performs_well_on.description: X (a model/method) performs well on Y (a task/domain), where Y is the task or domain where X demonstrates competence.
performs_well_on.semantic_boundary: Use performs_well_on only when a specific method is explicitly credited with success on a task/domain; not for general capability claims, benchmark results, or co-occurrence.

no_consistent_winner.description: X (a method/approach) and Y (another method/approach) are compared, where neither consistently outperforms the other across settings or conditions, indicating a tie or lack of clear dominance.
no_consistent_winner.semantic_boundary: Use when a comparison explicitly states neither method wins overall; not for single-result wins, equal performance on one metric, or claims of superiority.

works_better_with.description: X (a method/approach) works better or is more effective when combined with or used in conjunction with Y (another method/approach), indicating a synergistic or conditional improvement.
works_better_with.semantic_boundary: Use when X is claimed to be more effective *because of* Y, not merely when X and Y are used together or compared; excludes co-occurrence and causal dependence.

motivated_by_concept.description: X (a method/approach) is motivated by or draws conceptual inspiration from Y (a concept, principle, or established practice in a related domain), where Y provides the underlying idea but X is not a direct technical extension, implementation, or mere background citation.
motivated_by_concept.semantic_boundary: Use when X’s design is conceptually inspired by Y, but X is not a direct implementation, extension, or mere citation of Y.

selects_example.description: X (a method/process) selects or chooses Y (an example/instance) from a set of candidates based on some criterion, where Y is the chosen item.
selects_example.semantic_boundary: Use when X explicitly picks Y from a candidate set; NOT when X merely uses, includes, or is associated with Y.

uses_tool_on_data.description: X (a method/tool) is applied to or used on Y (a dataset/data artifact) for processing, normalization, or evaluation, where Y is the data being processed and X is the tool performing the operation.
uses_tool_on_data.semantic_boundary: Use this when a method/tool actively transforms or evaluates a dataset; NOT when it merely creates, describes, or is co-listed with the data.

eliminates_need_for.description: X (a method/approach) eliminates or removes the need for Y (another method/approach), where X makes Y unnecessary or redundant.
eliminates_need_for.semantic_boundary: Applies when X actively makes Y unnecessary, not when X merely improves, replaces, or coexists with Y as an alternative.

pretrained_on_corpus.description: X (a model) is pretrained on Y (a corpus/dataset), where the pretraining objective is to maximize the likelihood of the data in Y, and Y provides the training signal for X's initialization.
pretrained_on_corpus.semantic_boundary: Pretrained_on_corpus applies when a model's initial weights are trained on a specific dataset, not when a model is merely evaluated, fine-tuned, or co-mentioned with a corpus.

provides_property.description: X (a method/approach) provides or offers Y (a property or characteristic) as a benefit or outcome, where the property is a qualitative advantage.
provides_property.semantic_boundary: Use when a method explicitly yields a qualitative advantage (e.g., robustness, efficiency), not when it merely enables or depends on a property.

fine_tunes_on_data.description: X (a model/method) is fine-tuned on Y (a dataset/data source), where the fine-tuning adapts X's pretrained weights using Y's examples. This is distinct from pretrained_on_corpus (which covers initial pretraining) and trains_with_data (which covers training on data produced by another method).
fine_tunes_on_data.semantic_boundary: Fine-tuning applies only when Y is a dataset used to update X's pretrained weights, not when Y is a corpus for initial pretraining or data produced by another method.

utilizes_pretrained_model.description: X (a method/approach) utilizes or leverages Y (a pretrained model/PLM) as a resource or foundation, where Y's pretrained capabilities are employed by X but X is not necessarily based on Y's architecture or trained on Y's outputs. This is weaker than based_on_pretraining (which requires Y's pretraining to directly enable X's design) and distinct from uses_tool (which is for software libraries).
utilizes_pretrained_model.semantic_boundary: Utilizes_pretrained_model applies when X employs Y's pretrained weights/capabilities, but not when Y's pretraining defines X's core design (based_on_pretraining) or Y is a software tool (uses_tool).

approximates_target.description: X (a method/model) approximates or estimates Y (a target distribution, output, or value), where Y is the reference that X aims to match or approach.
approximates_target.semantic_boundary: Use when X is a method/model explicitly aiming to match Y as a reference, not when X merely predicts, measures, or depends on Y.

uses_hardware.description: X (a method/experiment) uses or runs on Y (hardware/GPU resources), where Y provides the computational infrastructure for X's execution.
uses_hardware.semantic_boundary: X applies when Y is the physical computational infrastructure (e.g., GPU, cluster) executing X, NOT when Y is a dataset, software library, or method that X merely references or depends on.

defines_task_as_generation.description: X (a task/problem) is defined as the generation of Y (an output/answer) from Z (an input/context), where the task's objective is to produce Y given Z.
defines_task_as_generation.semantic_boundary: Use when a task is explicitly defined by its output and input, not when describing a process, capability, or mere association between task and artifacts.

fails_to_process.description: X (a method/process) fails to process or handle Y (a specific input, data, or context), where the failure is a specific operational shortcoming rather than a general limitation.
fails_to_process.semantic_boundary: Applies when a specific method/process encounters a concrete input it cannot handle; NOT for general limitations, failed outcomes, or when the method is absent.

trains_policy_network.description: X (a method/approach) trains or optimizes Y (a policy network) to generate outputs, where Y is the policy component being trained by X's reinforcement learning procedure.
trains_policy_network.semantic_boundary: Use when X explicitly optimizes or trains Y as a policy network via RL; not for Y being a general method, a loss function, or merely used by X.

transfers_across_models.description: X (a learned artifact/prompt) transfers or generalizes from Y (one model) to Z (other models), where the artifact maintains effectiveness across different models.
transfers_across_models.semantic_boundary: Transfers across models applies when the same artifact is explicitly evaluated on multiple distinct models; NOT when a method is merely compared or benchmarked across models.

possesses_shared_structure.description: X (a set of models) possesses or exhibits Y (a shared structure/pattern), where the structure is common across the models.
possesses_shared_structure.semantic_boundary: X = a shared structure explicitly claimed common across multiple models, NOT a property of one model or a mere co-occurrence of features.

formulates_as_rl_problem.description: X (a method/approach) formulates or frames Y (a task/problem) as an instance of Z (a reinforcement learning problem), where the formulation recasts the task in RL terms (state, action, reward, policy) rather than merely defining the task's input-output structure.
formulates_as_rl_problem.semantic_boundary: Applies when X explicitly recasts Y in RL terms (state/action/reward/policy), not when X merely uses RL as a tool or defines Y’s input-output structure.

uses_implementation.description: X (a method/approach) uses or relies on Y (a software implementation/codebase) to execute its operations, where Y is a concrete code implementation rather than a general tool or library.
uses_implementation.semantic_boundary: X uses Y as its actual codebase to run, NOT Y being a general tool/library, a component, or a co-listed dependency.

experiments_on_dataset.description: X (a work/study) conducts experiments on Y (a dataset/domain), where Y is the data or domain used for experimentation. This is distinct from explores_setting (which requires a named setting/regime) and from uses_tool_on_data (which requires a tool actively transforming data).
experiments_on_dataset.semantic_boundary: Apply when a method explicitly runs experiments on a dataset/domain; not when merely exploring a named setting, nor when a tool actively transforms data.

models_context_with_vectors.description: X (a method/approach) models or represents Y (a set of context words/tokens) using Z (continuous vectors/embeddings), where the representation is a design choice for how the context is encoded.
models_context_with_vectors.semantic_boundary: Use when a method explicitly encodes context words as vectors; not for co-occurrence counts, attention weights, or vector similarity between separate items.

uses_parameter.description: X (a method/approach) uses or sets Y (a parameter/hyperparameter) as part of its configuration or operation, where Y is a numerical or categorical setting that controls X's behavior.
uses_parameter.semantic_boundary: Applies when X explicitly configures or operates via Y, not when Y merely describes X’s type, output, or co-occurring setting.

points_to_survey.description: X (a work/chapter) points readers to Y (an existing survey/review) as a resource for further reading, where Y is cited as a reference for additional information rather than as background, motivation, or a technical predecessor.
points_to_survey.semantic_boundary: Apply when a work explicitly directs readers to a survey/review for further reading, not when citing it as background, motivation, or technical foundation.

organizes_along_axes.description: X (a work/perspective) organizes or structures Y (a set of entities) along Z (a set of axes/dimensions), where the organization is the primary contribution and the axes are the criteria used for categorization.
organizes_along_axes.semantic_boundary: Use when the organizer’s main act is categorizing entities by explicit criteria, not merely listing, comparing, or causally linking them.

reformulates_as_generation.description: X (a non-generation task) is reformulated as Y (a generation problem) by providing Z (prompts/input texts), where the reformulation recasts the task's output as generated text.
reformulates_as_generation.semantic_boundary: Apply when a task is redefined as text generation via explicit prompts, not when the task merely uses generation as a step or is a co-listing of task and output.

explores_variants_in.description: X (a model/approach) has been explored in or instantiated by Y (a set of specific models/implementations), where Y are concrete realizations of X's design.
explores_variants_in.semantic_boundary: Use when Y are concrete implementations or instantiations of X’s design, not when Y are merely variants, alternatives, or competing approaches to X.

maps_to_output_space.description: X (an answer space) is mapped to Y (an output space), where the mapping defines how elements of the answer space correspond to or are transformed into the output space. This is a structural relationship between two spaces, distinct from a general influence or dependence.
maps_to_output_space.semantic_boundary: Maps_to_output_space applies when one property space is explicitly transformed or converted into another, NOT when they merely co-occur, influence each other, or share a dependency.

distills_knowledge_from.description: X (a model/method) distills knowledge from Y (a dataset, model, or ensemble), where the distillation transfers knowledge from Y to X, typically by training X on Y's outputs or annotations.
distills_knowledge_from.semantic_boundary: Use when X is trained on Y’s outputs/annotations to transfer knowledge; NOT for mere evaluation, fine-tuning on raw data, or ensembling without explicit teacher-student training.

categorizes_by_parameter.description: X (a set of strategies/methods) is categorized or organized based on Y (a parameter or design dimension), where the parameter determines the classification of the strategies.
categorizes_by_parameter.semantic_boundary: Use when a method is explicitly grouped or classified by a parameter, not when the parameter merely influences or describes the method’s behavior.

prone_to_failure.description: X (a method/model) is prone to or susceptible to Y (a failure mode/phenomenon), where Y is a known risk or tendency of X under certain conditions, but not a specific input that X fails to process.
prone_to_failure.semantic_boundary: Applies when Y is a known risk or tendency of X, not a specific input X fails to process, nor a co-occurring limitation.

is_instance_of_broader_category.description: X (a method/approach) is a specific instance or example of Y (a broader category/class of methods), where Y is a general category that encompasses X and other similar methods.
is_instance_of_broader_category.semantic_boundary: Use when X is a specific named method falling under a broader method category, not when X and Y are alternatives, synonyms, or a method and its component.

conceptually_introduces.description: X (a work/study) conceptually introduces or presents Y (a set of paradigms/categories) as a framing, where the introduction is a conceptual exposition rather than a technical extension, definition, or comparison.
conceptually_introduces.semantic_boundary: Applies when X explicitly frames Y as a new conceptual lens or paradigm, not when X merely defines, extends, compares, or technically implements Y.

calibrates_based_on.description: X (a method/approach) calibrates or adjusts Y (a probability distribution or output) based on Z (a prior likelihood or contextual information), where the calibration uses the prior as a reference to correct or refine the output. This is distinct from influences (which is about causal dependence) and from uses_technique (which is about employing a technique).
calibrates_based_on.semantic_boundary: Apply only when a method explicitly adjusts a distribution/output using a prior as a reference, not for mere causal influence or technique employment.

increases_popularity_of.description: X (a method/approach) increases the popularity or adoption of Y (another method/approach), where X's success or prevalence drives broader interest in Y.
increases_popularity_of.semantic_boundary: Applies when X actively causes broader adoption of Y, not when X merely precedes, co-occurs with, or is a prerequisite for Y.

comparative_study_of.description: X (a work/study) presents a comparative study of Y (a set of methods/approaches), where the comparison is the primary contribution and the methods are systematically evaluated against each other.
comparative_study_of.semantic_boundary: Apply when the paper's main contribution is systematically comparing methods; not when methods are merely listed, combined, or one is applied to another.

compares_to_baseline.description: X (a method/approach) is compared against Y (a baseline or control condition) where Y is a simple, non-learned baseline (e.g., random, majority class, noun-only) used as a reference point to validate X's effectiveness. This is distinct from compares (which requires parallel alternatives or theory-vs-experiment) and from improves_over (which requires a performance claim).
compares_to_baseline.semantic_boundary: Use only when Y is a simple, non-learned baseline (e.g., random, majority, noun-only) and no performance metric is stated; otherwise use improves_over or compares.

enables_investigation_of.description: X (a method/approach) enables or allows the investigation of Y (a capability/behavior), where Y is the research question or ability being studied through X's design. This is distinct from serves_purpose (which is about achieving a goal) and from influences (which is about causal dependence).
enables_investigation_of.semantic_boundary: Use when X’s design directly enables studying Y as a capability/behavior; not for achieving goals (serves_purpose) or causal influence (influences).

compares_generated_data.description: X (a method/approach) is compared against Y (data generated by another method/approach), where the comparison evaluates the quality or characteristics of the generated data against a reference or alternative generation method.
compares_generated_data.semantic_boundary: Applies when a method is evaluated against data produced by another method, not when comparing methods themselves or their outputs as co-equal artifacts.

uses_api_for_generation.description: X (a method/process) uses Y (an API or external service) to generate or produce data, where the API is a specific external tool employed for data generation.
uses_api_for_generation.semantic_boundary: Use this when a method explicitly calls an external API/service to produce data, NOT when it merely depends on or co-occurs with another method.

compares_against_human_judgment.description: X (responses from a model/LLM) is compared against Y (human annotator decisions) to evaluate the model's efficacy, where the human judgment serves as the reference standard.
compares_against_human_judgment.semantic_boundary: Applies when a model output is explicitly scored or validated against human labels as ground truth, not when comparing two independent methods or model variants.

compares_models_on_dataset.description: X (a set of models) is compared against Y (another set of models) on Z (a dataset), where the comparison is the primary activity and the dataset is the evaluation context.
compares_models_on_dataset.semantic_boundary: Applies when two model sets are explicitly evaluated against each other on a shared dataset, not when one model is simply applied to a dataset or models are listed without comparison.

observes_departure_from_assumption.description: X (a work/study) observes or reports that Y (a finding/result) departs from or contradicts Z (an initial assumption/hypothesis), where the departure is an empirical observation rather than a causal claim or comparison.
observes_departure_from_assumption.semantic_boundary: Applies when X explicitly states that observed Y deviates from prior assumption Z; not for causal claims, comparisons, or mere co-occurrence of Y and Z.

unable_to_investigate.description: X (a work/study) is unable to investigate or explore Y (a scope/scale of models or phenomena) due to resource or other constraints, where the limitation is about the breadth of what could be studied, not a specific input failure. This is distinct from fails_to_process (which is about a concrete input that cannot be handled) and from constrained_by_resource (which focuses on the constraint itself).
unable_to_investigate.semantic_boundary: Applies when a work/study cannot explore a breadth of models/phenomena due to constraints, NOT when a specific input fails (fails_to_process) or when the constraint itself is the focus (constrained_by_resource).

emerges_in_model.description: X (a capability/ability) emerges in or appears at Y (a model/scale), where the capability is observed to arise at a specific model size or configuration. This is distinct from performs_well_on (which is about a model performing well on a task) and from has_primitive_ability (which is about basic recognition abilities).
emerges_in_model.semantic_boundary: Use when a capability is claimed to first appear at a specific model scale/size, not when a model merely performs well on a task or has a basic recognition ability.

aligns_with_human_judgment.description: X (a model/method) aligns with or matches Y (human judgment/annotations), where the alignment is about consistency between model outputs and human evaluations. This is distinct from compares_against_human_judgment (which is about explicit comparison/evaluation) and from performs_similarly_with_exception (which is about method-to-method comparison).
aligns_with_human_judgment.semantic_boundary: Applies when a model's outputs are measured against human ratings for agreement, not when comparing methods or explicitly evaluating model performance.

compares_consistency_between.description: X (a set of models/methods) is compared against Y (another set, e.g., human experts) in terms of consistency or agreement, where the comparison focuses on the stability or uniformity of outputs rather than raw performance. This is distinct from compares_models_on_dataset (which requires a shared dataset as evaluation context) and from improves_over (which requires a performance claim).
compares_consistency_between.semantic_boundary: Use when the claim is about agreement/stability between two method sets, not performance on a shared dataset (compares_models_on_dataset) and not superiority (improves_over).

provides_evidence_for.description: X (a study/analysis) provides or offers Y (empirical evidence or findings) about Z (a subject or phenomenon), where the evidence is the contribution of the work. This is distinct from provides_property (which is about a method providing a qualitative advantage) and from reports_statistics (which is about reporting quantitative summaries).
provides_evidence_for.semantic_boundary: Applies when a study/analysis explicitly contributes empirical evidence or findings about a subject, not when a method offers a qualitative advantage or when quantitative summaries are reported.

evaluates_against_human_labels.description: X (a method/model) is evaluated against Y (human labels/annotations) as a reference standard, where the evaluation compares model outputs to human-provided ground truth or judgments.
evaluates_against_human_labels.semantic_boundary: Applies when a method is explicitly compared to human labels as ground truth; not for comparing methods to each other or to non-human benchmarks.

costs_less_than.description: X (a model/method) is less expensive than Y (another model/method), where the comparison is about relative cost or resource expenditure.
costs_less_than.semantic_boundary: Use when one method is explicitly stated or implied as cheaper than another; not for equal cost, cost-effectiveness, or non-comparative mentions of price.

compares_metrics_equivalence.description: X (a metric/measure) is compared with Y (another metric/measure) to establish their equivalence or identity, where the comparison is about the statistical agreement between two different measurement approaches.
compares_metrics_equivalence.semantic_boundary: Applies when two metrics are explicitly tested for statistical equivalence or agreement (e.g., Bland-Altman, correlation), NOT when one metric merely co-occurs with another or is defined by it.

observes_similar_performance_range.description: X (a method/model) and Y (another method/model) are observed to perform within the same range or exhibit similar values on a metric, where the observation is about comparable performance levels without claiming superiority or inferiority.
observes_similar_performance_range.semantic_boundary: Use when two methods are explicitly reported as having similar or overlapping performance; NOT when one is claimed better, worse, or when they are merely listed together without a comparative observation.

consistency_depends_on_task.description: X (a model/method) exhibits task-dependent consistency patterns, where the consistency or agreement of X varies across different tasks Y1, Y2... (e.g., binary classification, sentiment analysis, numerical prediction), indicating that the relationship between model sophistication and consistency is not universal but task-specific.
consistency_depends_on_task.semantic_boundary: Applies when a model’s consistency is explicitly compared across multiple tasks, showing task-specific variation—not a general property of the model, nor a simple co-occurrence of tasks.

provides_more_consistent_measurement.description: X (a method/tool) provides more consistent or reliable measurements than Y (another method/tool), where the comparison is specifically about measurement consistency or stability, not overall performance.
provides_more_consistent_measurement.semantic_boundary: Applies when the claim explicitly contrasts measurement consistency/stability between methods, not overall performance, accuracy, or general superiority.

correlates_with.description: X (a property/characteristic) correlates with Y (another property/characteristic), where the correlation is a statistical relationship between two continuous or ordinal variables, not a causal dependence or a comparison of methods.
correlates_with.semantic_boundary: Use for statistical association between two measured variables; not for causal/functional dependence, method comparison, or mere co-occurrence in text.

consistency_varies_with_model.description: X (a model/method) exhibits consistency patterns that vary with Y (another model/method), where the consistency of X is compared against Y across tasks or metrics, showing that model advancement does not guarantee improved consistency.
consistency_varies_with_model.semantic_boundary: Applies when consistency of model1 is measured relative to model2 across tasks/metrics, NOT when comparing standalone performance or ranking models by accuracy.

examines_influence_on.description: X (a work/study) examines or investigates the influence of Y (a factor/variable) on Z (an outcome/behavior), where the examination is the primary activity and the relationship between Y and Z is the focus. This is distinct from influences (which states a causal dependence) and from measures (which involves instrumentation).
examines_influence_on.semantic_boundary: Use when the text explicitly describes a study or work investigating how one factor affects another, not when it asserts the influence as fact or measures it with instruments.

uses_llm_as_annotator.description: X (a method/process) uses Y (an LLM or AI system) as an annotator or judge to assign labels/scores to data, where Y's outputs are used as annotations or ratings for filtering or selection. This is distinct from uses_tool (which is for software libraries/toolkits) and from uses_api_for_generation (which is about generating data via API).
uses_llm_as_annotator.semantic_boundary: Apply when an LLM/AI system outputs labels/scores used as annotations for filtering/selection, not when it generates data or when a software library/toolkit is used.

differs_from_in_evaluation.description: X (a method/approach) differs from Y (another method/approach) specifically in terms of evaluation methodology or experimental setup, where the difference is about how the methods are evaluated rather than their underlying mechanism or design. This is distinct from contrasts_with (which is about fundamental mechanism differences) and from compares (which is about putting methods side by side).
differs_from_in_evaluation.semantic_boundary: Applies when the claimed difference is specifically about evaluation setup (metrics, datasets, protocols), not about how the methods work or a general side-by-side comparison.

suggests_future_extension.description: X (a method/work) suggests or recommends extending to Y (a domain, setting, or use case) as future work, where the extension is proposed but not implemented or demonstrated.
suggests_future_extension.semantic_boundary: Apply when a method/work explicitly proposes extending to a new domain or use case as future work, NOT when the extension is already implemented, demonstrated, or merely co-mentioned.

serves_as_evaluation_category.description: X (a task category) serves as or represents Y (a domain/application area) in the context of evaluation, where the task category is chosen because it is representative of the domain's critical tasks.
serves_as_evaluation_category.semantic_boundary: Use when a task category is explicitly chosen to represent a domain’s critical tasks in evaluation, not when merely listing tasks or stating a domain’s general relevance.

informed_by_theory.description: X (a design artifact/method) is informed by or grounded in Y (a theory/framework), where the theory provides the conceptual foundation for the artifact's design. This is distinct from based_on_perspective (which is about conceptual inspiration) and from motivated_by_concept (which is about motivation), as it specifically involves a kernel theory informing a design artifact.
informed_by_theory.semantic_boundary: Apply when a named theory explicitly shapes the artifact’s design logic, not when it merely inspires, motivates, or is co-listed with it.

contributes_knowledge_to.description: X (a work/approach) contributes to Y (a body of knowledge or design principles), where the contribution is about adding to a knowledge base or set of principles. This is distinct from provides_evidence_for (which is about empirical evidence) and from provides_property (which is about qualitative advantages).
contributes_knowledge_to.semantic_boundary: Applies when a method explicitly extends or refines a stated body of knowledge or principles, not when it merely demonstrates empirical support or claims a qualitative advantage.

contributes_positively_to.description: X (a method/component) contributes positively to Y (a task/outcome), where the contribution is a beneficial effect on the task's performance or success.
contributes_positively_to.semantic_boundary: Use only when a method/component actively improves a task’s outcome; not for mere association, co-occurrence, or neutral/negative effects.

designs_agents_based_on_error_categories.description: X (a set of agents/roles) is designed based on Y (a set of error categories or a prior work's taxonomy), where the design of the agents is directly motivated by and structured around the error categories identified in prior work. This is distinct from based_on_perspective (which is about conceptual inspiration) and from inspired_by_technique (which is about methodological inspiration) — here the design is a direct instantiation of the error taxonomy into agent roles.
designs_agents_based_on_error_categories.semantic_boundary: Use when agent roles are directly derived from specific error types, not when errors merely inspire or co-occur with the design.

formalizes_task.description: X (a work/paper) formalizes or defines Y (a task/problem) as a formal problem statement, where the formalization establishes the task's scope, inputs, outputs, and evaluation criteria. This is distinct from defines_problem_setting (which frames a broader setting) and from formulates_task (which is about conceptual framing).
formalizes_task.semantic_boundary: Apply when a paper explicitly states a task’s formal inputs, outputs, and evaluation criteria; not for broader problem framing or conceptual task formulation.

uses_metric.description: X (a method/approach) uses or reports Y (a metric/indicator) as an evaluation measure or performance indicator, where Y is a quantitative metric used to assess X's output or behavior.
uses_metric.semantic_boundary: Applies when a method explicitly reports a quantitative metric as its evaluation result, not when the metric merely describes a property of the method's output.

trains_components_on_data.description: X (a method/approach) trains individual components or modules of Y (a model/system) on Z (a dataset/data source), where the training is component-specific rather than whole-model training. This is distinct from fine_tunes_on_data (which applies to the whole model's pretrained weights) and from trains_with_data (which is about training on data produced by another method).
trains_components_on_data.semantic_boundary: Use this pattern only when a specific component/module of a model is trained on data, not the whole model (fine_tunes_on_data) and not on data produced by another method (trains_with_data).

defines_dataset_purpose.description: X (a dataset) is created for or serves the purpose of Y (a task/domain), where the dataset is designed to support or enable the task. This is distinct from serves_purpose (which is about a method achieving a goal) and from defines_task_as_generation (which is about input-output structure).
defines_dataset_purpose.semantic_boundary: Use only when a dataset is explicitly created or designated for a task/domain, not when a method achieves a goal or when defining input-output structure.

shares_hyperparameters_with.description: X (a model/method) shares the same hyperparameter configuration as Y (another model/method), where the hyperparameters (e.g., pre-training hyperparameters) are explicitly stated to be identical or matched between the two, without claiming X is based on, derived from, or follows the methodology of Y.
shares_hyperparameters_with.semantic_boundary: Applies only when hyperparameters are explicitly stated as identical or matched between two methods, NOT when one is derived from, based on, or follows the other's methodology.

evaluates_tasks_as_generation.description: X (a set of tasks/datasets) is evaluated by modeling all tasks as Y (a generation format, e.g., text-to-text) using Z (a set of generative models), where the evaluation reformulates the tasks into a unified generation framework.
evaluates_tasks_as_generation.semantic_boundary: Use when tasks are reformulated into a unified generation format and scored by generative models; NOT for classification, retrieval, or task-specific metrics.

creates_benchmark.description: X (a work/study) creates or introduces Y (a benchmark/dataset) for evaluating Z (a set of capabilities/tasks), where the benchmark is a concrete artifact produced by the work. This is distinct from introduces_benchmark (which requires the benchmark to be the primary contribution and standardize tasks) and from creates_data (which is for general data artifacts, not evaluation benchmarks).
creates_benchmark.semantic_boundary: Use when the benchmark is a concrete artifact the work produces, not merely introduced or standardized, and it evaluates specific capabilities—not general data creation.

trades_based_on_news_timing.description: X (a trading action) is executed based on the timing of Y (a news event/regime), where the timing of the news determines when the trade is initiated or executed.
trades_based_on_news_timing.semantic_boundary: Use when the trade’s timing is explicitly set by a news event/regime, not when news merely influences the trade’s direction or magnitude.

evaluates_with_statistical_measures.description: X (a model/method) is evaluated using Y (a set of statistical measures), where the measures are quantitative metrics used to assess the model's performance.
evaluates_with_statistical_measures.semantic_boundary: Use when a method is explicitly assessed via quantitative metrics (e.g., accuracy, F1), not when metrics merely describe properties or when methods are compared without stated evaluation measures.

compares_against_conventional_method.description: X (a set of models/methods) is compared against Y (a conventional/traditional method) in terms of performance or output, where the comparison is between modern/learned methods and a traditional baseline, and the conventional method serves as a reference point for evaluating the modern methods' effectiveness.
compares_against_conventional_method.semantic_boundary: Applies when modern/learned methods are explicitly evaluated against a traditional baseline; NOT for comparing two modern methods or two conventional methods.

declares_no_conflict.description: X (a work/team) declares or states Y (a conflict-of-interest disclosure or absence of competing interests), where the declaration is a formal statement about the work's independence from financial or personal influences.
declares_no_conflict.semantic_boundary: Applies when a method explicitly states a conflict-of-interest or its absence; not when merely listing funding sources or declaring author contributions.

compares_against_aggregate_baseline.description: X (a method/model) is compared against Y (an aggregate or collective baseline representing the best or typical performance of a group of methods), where the comparison evaluates X against a summary or representative performance level rather than a single named method. This is distinct from compares_to_baseline (which requires a simple, non-learned baseline) and from improves_over (which requires a specific named baseline).
compares_against_aggregate_baseline.semantic_boundary: Use when the baseline is a group summary (e.g., average, best-of, ensemble), not a single named method or a simple non-learned baseline.

incorporates_knowledge_during_training.description: X (a model/method) incorporates or integrates Y (a body of knowledge/domain expertise) during its training process, where the knowledge is embedded into the model's parameters or representations as part of the training objective. This is distinct from based_on_pretraining (which requires a pretrained model as foundation) and from trains_with_data (which is about training on data produced by another method).
incorporates_knowledge_during_training.semantic_boundary: Applies when knowledge is explicitly encoded into model parameters via training, not when using a pretrained model or training on data from another method.

evaluated_by_metrics.description: X (a task/benchmark) is evaluated using Y (a set of metrics), where the metrics are the standard evaluation measures for the task. This is distinct from uses_metric (which requires a method using a metric) and from evaluates_with_statistical_measures (which requires a model being evaluated). Here the task itself is the subject being evaluated.
evaluated_by_metrics.semantic_boundary: Apply when the task/benchmark itself is the subject being measured by standard metrics, not when a method or model is being evaluated.

introduces_method_for_task.description: X (a work/study) introduces Y (a method/approach) specifically designed for or targeting Z (a task/domain), where the method is the primary contribution and the task is the domain it addresses. This is distinct from introduces_benchmark (which requires a benchmark artifact) and from formulates_task (which is about framing a task) — here the contribution is a method aimed at a task.
introduces_method_for_task.semantic_boundary: Apply when the paper’s primary contribution is a method/approach explicitly aimed at a task/domain, not when the contribution is a benchmark artifact or merely framing the task itself.

motivates_future_research_on.description: X (a finding/direction) naturally leads to or motivates future research on Y (a related topic/area), where the motivation is a logical consequence of the current work, distinct from serves_purpose (which requires an explicit goal) and from suggests_future_extension (which is about extending to new domains).
motivates_future_research_on.semantic_boundary: Applies when the finding logically implies a need for future work on a method, not when an explicit goal exists (serves_purpose) or when extending to a new domain (suggests_future_extension).

accelerates_evolution_of.description: X (a development/trend) accelerates or speeds up the evolution of Y (a related technology/approach), where the acceleration is about hastening development, distinct from increases_popularity_of (which is about adoption) and from influences (which is about causal dependence).
accelerates_evolution_of.semantic_boundary: Apply when X actively speeds up the development of Y, not when X merely increases Y's adoption or when X causally influences Y without hastening its progress.

organizes_under_principle.description: X (a work/study) organizes or structures Y (a set of themes/entities) under Z (a set of principles/axes), where the principles serve as the organizing framework and the themes are categorized under each principle. This is distinct from organizes_along_axes (which organizes along continuous dimensions) and from based_on_perspective (which is about conceptual foundation).
organizes_under_principle.semantic_boundary: Use when a method explicitly groups or categorizes properties under named principles; not for continuous axes (organizes_along_axes) or conceptual foundations (based_on_perspective).

summarizes_ethics_in_themes.description: X (a work/review) summarizes or organizes Y (a set of ethical considerations) into Z (a set of themes/categories), where the themes are the organizing structure for the ethical discussion. This is distinct from organizes_along_axes (which requires explicit axes) and from explores_setting (which requires a named setting).
summarizes_ethics_in_themes.semantic_boundary: Apply when ethical points are grouped under named themes (e.g., "privacy," "fairness") as the organizing structure, not when axes or a named setting drive the organization.

outlines_directions_for_domain.description: X (a work/review) outlines or presents Y (methodological directions) for Z (a domain/regime), where the directions are proposed as future work in the context of the domain.
outlines_directions_for_domain.semantic_boundary: Applies when a work explicitly proposes future methodological directions for a domain, not when it merely describes, applies, or evaluates methods within that domain.

provides_insights_for.description: X (a method/paradigm) provides or offers insights into Y (a domain/application area), where the insights are about understanding how X can be applied or adapted to Y. This is distinct from contributes_knowledge_to (which is about adding to a body of knowledge) and from provides_property (which is about a qualitative advantage).
provides_insights_for.semantic_boundary: Use when X is a method/paradigm and Y is a domain it can be applied to, offering understanding of that application—not when X adds knowledge to Y or provides a qualitative advantage.

reports_performance_gap.description: X (a method/result) reports or exhibits a performance gap relative to Y (a reference/standard), where the gap is a quantitative difference in performance between two entities. This is distinct from improves_over (which requires one method to be better) and from compares (which is neutral).
reports_performance_gap.semantic_boundary: Apply when a specific quantitative performance difference is stated between measured and reference, not when one is merely better (improves_over) or when no gap is quantified (compares).

introduces_dataset_with_unique_attribute.description: X (a work/study) introduces Y (a dataset) with a unique attribute Z (a distinctive annotation or feature), where the dataset's contribution is its novel annotation scheme or unique characteristic. This is distinct from introduces_benchmark (which requires a benchmark artifact) and from introduces_method_for_task (which is about a method contribution).
introduces_dataset_with_unique_attribute.semantic_boundary: Applies when the paper explicitly claims the dataset’s novelty is a specific annotation or feature, not when it merely introduces a benchmark or a method for a task.

improves_with_increasing_shots.description: X (a method/approach) improves in performance as Y (a resource/input quantity, e.g., number of shots) increases, where the improvement is a monotonic or general trend tied to the resource level, distinct from improves_over (which compares two distinct methods) and from influences (which is a general dependence).
improves_with_increasing_shots.semantic_boundary: Use when a single method’s performance scales with a resource level; not for comparing two methods (improves_over) or general dependence (influences).

trains_on_foundation_model.description: X (a model) is trained on Y (a foundation model) as the base architecture, where Y provides the initial weights/architecture and X is trained further on domain-specific data. This is distinct from fine_tunes_on_data (which requires a dataset as the data source) and from based_on_pretraining (which requires the pretraining to directly enable X's design).
trains_on_foundation_model.semantic_boundary: Use when X's training explicitly starts from Y's weights/architecture, not when Y merely enables X's design or when training data is the source.

widely_used_for.description: X (a method/model) is widely used for or applied to Y (a task/domain), where the usage is a general, established practice rather than a specific technical dependency or comparison. This is distinct from uses_technique (which requires X to employ Y as a technique) and from performs_well_on (which requires a performance claim).
widely_used_for.semantic_boundary: Apply when X is established as a common/general tool for Y, not when X employs Y as a technique, nor when a performance claim about X on Y is made.

adapts_pretrained_model.description: X (a method/approach) adapts or fine-tunes Y (a pretrained model/LLM) for a specific task or domain, where Y's pretrained capabilities are leveraged and adjusted for X's target application. This is distinct from based_on_pretraining (which requires Y's pretraining to directly enable X's design) and from fine_tunes_on_data (which requires a dataset as the adaptation source).
adapts_pretrained_model.semantic_boundary: Apply when a method explicitly modifies or fine-tunes a pretrained model’s weights for a new task, not when the model merely enables the method’s design or when training data is the adaptation source.

applied_to_domain.description: X (a method/technology) is applied to or used in Y (a domain/application area), where the application is a general usage context rather than a specific task or technical dependency.
applied_to_domain.semantic_boundary: Applied to domain when X is a method/technology used in a general field (e.g., ML in healthcare), NOT a specific task (e.g., classification) or technical dependency (e.g., X requires Y).

provides_insight_for.description: X (a method/approach/analysis) provides or offers Y (insights, understanding, or supplementary analysis) for Z (a purpose, task, or domain), where the insight is a contribution that supports or enhances the purpose. This is distinct from serves_purpose (which requires X to be an action aimed at achieving Y as its goal) and from provides_property (which is about a qualitative advantage).
provides_insight_for.semantic_boundary: Applies when X yields an insight (analysis, understanding) that supports Z, not when X is an action achieving Z (serves_purpose) or a qualitative advantage (provides_property).

achieves_approach_for.description: X (a method/approach) achieves or enables Y (a more holistic approach or perspective) for Z (a task/domain), where the achievement is about reaching a broader or more integrated approach to the task. This is distinct from serves_purpose (which requires X to be an action aimed at Y as its goal) and from provides_property (which is about a qualitative advantage).
achieves_approach_for.semantic_boundary: Use when X is a method that yields a broader, integrated approach Y for task Z, not when X is an action aimed at Y as a goal, nor a qualitative advantage.

reveals_early_warning.description: X (a method/analysis) reveals or exposes Y (an early warning signal or indicator of a condition), where the analysis uncovers a predictive sign of a future state. This is distinct from applied_to_domain (which is about general usage context) and from provides_evidence_for (which is about empirical evidence for a subject).
reveals_early_warning.semantic_boundary: Use when a method explicitly uncovers a predictive sign of a future condition, not when it merely applies to a domain or provides general evidence for that condition.

struggles_to_generalize.description: X (a method/approach) struggles to or fails to generalize or integrate knowledge across Y (a set of tasks/domains), where the limitation is about cross-task transfer rather than processing a specific input. This is distinct from fails_to_process (which requires a concrete input that cannot be handled) and from unable_to_investigate (which is about scope of study).
struggles_to_generalize.semantic_boundary: This pattern applies when a method fails across tasks/domains, not when it fails on a specific input or when the limitation is merely outside the study's scope.

has_limitation.description: X (a model/method) has a limitation Y (a shortcoming or constraint), where the limitation is a general weakness or inability of the model, distinct from prone_to_failure (which is about a specific failure mode) and from focuses_on_limitation (which is about a work addressing a limitation).
has_limitation.semantic_boundary: Use when a method is explicitly stated to have a general weakness or constraint, not when describing a specific failure instance or when a work addresses that limitation.

compares_prompting_strategies.description: X (a prompting strategy) is compared against Y (another prompting strategy) and Z (a third prompting strategy) in terms of their effect on a model's performance, where the comparison is a listing of alternative strategies without a specific performance claim.
compares_prompting_strategies.semantic_boundary: Applies when three prompting strategies are listed as alternatives without any performance comparison; NOT for pairwise comparisons or when a specific performance claim is made.

evaluates_performance_in_domain.description: X (a model/method) is evaluated or assessed in the context of Y (a domain/application area), where the evaluation is about the model's performance within that specific domain.
evaluates_performance_in_domain.semantic_boundary: Use when the model’s performance is explicitly judged within a domain; not for mere co-occurrence, capability listing, or domain membership.

aims_to_generate_output.description: X (a method/approach) aims to or is designed to generate Y (a specific output or result), where the generation is the explicit goal or purpose of the method.
aims_to_generate_output.semantic_boundary: Use only when the method’s explicit purpose is to produce that output, not when it merely uses, evaluates, or co-occurs with it.

designs_prompt_for_domain.description: X (a work/study) designs or creates Y (a prompt/prompting strategy) specifically for Z (a domain/application area), where the design is tailored to the domain's requirements.
designs_prompt_for_domain.semantic_boundary: Applies when a work/study explicitly creates a prompt/prompting strategy for a named domain, not when it merely uses or evaluates prompts in that domain.

downloads_from_source.description: X (a method/work) downloads or retrieves Y (a data source/repository) as part of its data acquisition process, where Y is a specific external source (e.g., SEC EDGAR) from which data is obtained.
downloads_from_source.semantic_boundary: Applies when a method explicitly retrieves data from an external source, not when it merely references, cites, or processes data already obtained elsewhere.

provides_guidance_for.description: X (a work/survey) provides guidance or recommendations for Y (a decision process or application area), where the guidance is the primary contribution and Y is the domain or process being guided.
provides_guidance_for.semantic_boundary: Use when the work’s main output is actionable guidance for a specific process/domain, not when it merely evaluates, describes, or co-lists that target.

has_architectural_variants.description: X (a model/architecture) has Y1, Y2... as specific architectural variants or instantiations, where the variants share the core architecture but differ in specific design choices (e.g., encoder-only, decoder-only, encoder-decoder). This is distinct from composed_of (which is about structural parts) and from is_instance_of_broader_category (which is about a method being an instance of a category).
has_architectural_variants.semantic_boundary: Use when one method is a named architectural variant of another (e.g., encoder-only vs. decoder-only), not when describing structural parts or a method as a broader category instance.

compares_scores_on_metric.description: X (a method/model) is compared against Y (another method/model) based on their respective scores on a shared metric, where the comparison is explicitly quantified with score values.
compares_scores_on_metric.semantic_boundary: Applies only when both methods’ scores on the same metric are explicitly stated with numbers; not for qualitative comparisons or score mentions without both values.

suggests_alternative_when_unsatisfactory.description: X (a method/approach) is suggested as an alternative or fallback when Y (another method/approach) fails to produce satisfactory results, where the suggestion is conditional on Y's failure.
suggests_alternative_when_unsatisfactory.semantic_boundary: Applies when X is explicitly proposed as a fallback *because* Y failed, not merely as an alternative, replacement, or co-existing option.

mitigates_limitation.description: X (a method/approach) mitigates or addresses Y (a limitation/failure mode), where the mitigation is a proposed or implemented countermeasure to reduce the impact of Y. This is distinct from eliminates_need_for (which removes the need for another method) and from focuses_on_limitation (which is about a work targeting a limitation as motivation).
mitigates_limitation.semantic_boundary: Mitigates_limitation applies when X is a proposed or implemented countermeasure reducing Y’s impact, not when X removes Y’s need or merely targets Y as motivation.

proposes_framework_for.description: X (a work/study) proposes or presents Y (a structured framework/methodology) for addressing Z (a task/decision problem), where the framework is the primary contribution and provides a systematic approach to the task. This is distinct from introduces_method_for_task (which requires a specific method/approach rather than a framework) and from formulates_task (which frames the task itself).
proposes_framework_for.semantic_boundary: Use only when a work explicitly presents a structured framework as its main contribution to a task, not when it merely introduces a specific method or merely reframes the task itself.

uses_data_from_source.description: X (a method/model) uses data from Y (a data source/repository), where the data is sourced from Y for training or fine-tuning. This is distinct from downloads_from_source (which requires explicit retrieval) and from fine_tunes_on_data (which requires a dataset as the adaptation source).
uses_data_from_source.semantic_boundary: X applies when Y is explicitly cited as the data used for training/fine-tuning, NOT when Y is merely downloaded, hosted, or listed as a general resource.

introduces_benchmark_with_model_and_data.description: X (a work/study) introduces Y (a benchmark) along with Z (a model) and W (a dataset) as a unified contribution, where the benchmark, model, and dataset are jointly presented as the work's primary artifacts.
introduces_benchmark_with_model_and_data.semantic_boundary: Applies only when the same work jointly presents benchmark, model, and dataset as its core artifacts; not for separate papers or when one is merely used/evaluated.

is_among_largest_in_category.description: X (a dataset/resource) is among the largest in Y (a category of resources), where the claim is about relative size/scale within a category.
is_among_largest_in_category.semantic_boundary: Use when the claim explicitly ranks or compares X’s size/scale against others in Y, not when X is merely listed as a member or typical example of Y.

ranks_among_models.description: X (a model/method) is ranked or positioned among Y (a set of other models/methods) in terms of performance, where the claim is about X's relative standing (e.g., best, second, close second) within a group, without necessarily stating a specific quantitative gap. This is distinct from improves_over (which requires a pairwise superiority claim) and from compares_models_on_dataset (which requires a shared dataset as evaluation context).
ranks_among_models.semantic_boundary: Use when a claim ranks one method relative to others, but only if no specific dataset is named and no pairwise superiority is asserted.

studies_scaling_of.description: X (a work/study) studies or investigates the scaling behavior of Y (a set of models/architectures), where the study examines how performance or properties change with scale, and may derive guidelines or conclusions about scaling, distinct from examines_influence_on (which is about factor-outcome relationships) and from measures (which is about instrumentation).
studies_scaling_of.semantic_boundary: Applies when a study explicitly examines how performance or properties change with model scale, not when measuring a specific metric or testing a factor-outcome relationship.

trained_on_corpora.description: X (a model/method) is trained on Y (a collection of text corpora or data sources), where the training uses multiple heterogeneous sources (e.g., press releases, news articles, filings) as the training data.
trained_on_corpora.semantic_boundary: Use only when the model is explicitly trained on multiple heterogeneous text sources; not for single-corpus training or for models merely evaluated on or citing corpora.
